NODE-COR-01.title: Shared mutable state across calls
NODE-COR-01.cite: Python Programming FAQ, "Why are default values shared between objects?"; Python docs, `functools.lru_cache`
NODE-COR-01.fix: copy before mutating; keep per-request data on the request object or in `AsyncLocalStorage`; return tuples or frozen objects from caches.

NODE-COR-02.title: Duplicable external effect without an idempotency key
NODE-COR-02.fix: an `Idempotency-Key` derived from the business object (not random per attempt); record the attempt before calling; a unique constraint or processed-events table; disable the button while pending.

NODE-COR-03.title: In-place mutation and aliasing of caller-owned data
NODE-COR-03.cite: Python docs, `list.sort` (sorts in place, returns `None`); Python Programming FAQ, "How do I create a multidimensional list?"
NODE-COR-03.fix: `sorted()` / `toSorted()` / spread / `structuredClone` for nested data; build rows with a comprehension; filter into a new list instead of removing while iterating.

NODE-COR-04.title: Absent value dereferenced
NODE-COR-04.cite: Python docs, `re.match` (returns `None` when no match); MDN, `Array.prototype.find` (returns `undefined`)
NODE-COR-04.fix: check and return 404/422, or `next(it, default)`; enable `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`; replace `!` with a real check.

NODE-COR-05.title: Falsy value treated as missing
NODE-COR-05.cite: Python docs, "Truth Value Testing"; MDN, "Nullish coalescing operator (??)" and "Logical OR (||)"
NODE-COR-05.fix: compare to `None` / `undefined`; use `??`; parse flags explicitly.

NODE-COR-06.title: Boundary and pagination off-by-one
NODE-COR-06.cite: CWE-193 (off-by-one error); Python docs, "Common Sequence Operations" (slicing)
NODE-COR-06.fix: iterate over elements, not indexes; half-open ranges; fetch `size + 1` rows to detect a next page.

NODE-COR-07.title: Time zones and date arithmetic
NODE-COR-07.cite: Python docs, `datetime` ("Aware and Naive Objects") and "What's New in Python 3.12" (`utcnow` deprecation); PEP 615 (`zoneinfo`)
NODE-COR-07.fix: store and compare aware UTC instants; convert to the user's zone only for display (`zoneinfo`, `Intl.DateTimeFormat`); add calendar units with a library; `monotonic()` for durations.

NODE-COR-08.title: Floating point money
NODE-COR-08.cite: Python docs, "Floating Point Arithmetic: Issues and Limitations" and `decimal`; ECMA-262, Number type (IEEE 754 binary64)
NODE-COR-08.fix: integer minor units end to end, or `Decimal` built from strings with an explicit quantize and rounding mode; a decimal column in the database.

NODE-COR-09.title: Read-modify-write race
NODE-COR-09.fix: one atomic `UPDATE … SET x = x - $1 WHERE x >= $1`, `SELECT … FOR UPDATE`, a unique constraint with an upsert, Redis `INCR`; collect results then combine; a lock only as a last resort.

NODE-COR-10.title: Async work not awaited
NODE-COR-10.cite: Python docs, `asyncio.create_task` (save a reference to avoid a task disappearing mid-execution); Python docs, "Coroutines and Tasks"
NODE-COR-10.fix: `await` it, `Promise.all` it, or keep the task reference and attach a done callback that logs; `for … of` with `await` when order matters.

NODE-COR-14.title: Comparison semantics
NODE-COR-14.cite: MDN, `Array.prototype.sort` (default order is by UTF-16 string); ECMA-262, `IsLooselyEqual`
NODE-COR-14.fix: numeric comparator; test membership in a collection; `==` for values, `is` only for `None` and singletons.

NODE-COR-15.title: Unanchored or stateful regex
NODE-COR-15.fix: `re.fullmatch` or `\Z`; anchors on both ends; no `g`/`y` on shared regexes.

NODE-COR-16.title: Cache key missing a dimension
NODE-COR-16.cite: TanStack Query docs, "Query Keys"; RFC 9111 §4.1 (`Vary`) and §5.2.2.7 (`private`)
NODE-COR-16.fix: include every input in the key; do not cache per-user responses in shared caches; `Cache-Control: private` plus `Vary` for HTTP; call `invalidateQueries` after mutations.

NODE-COR-53.title: Syntax or API newer than the supported Node version
NODE-COR-53.cite: Node.js docs, per-API "History" tables; MDN, browser and runtime compatibility tables
NODE-COR-53.fix: raise `engines` and the CI matrix together, or use the compatible form.

NODE-COR-60.title: Process-local cache invalidated only in the process that wrote
NODE-COR-60.cite: Node.js docs, `cluster` (workers are separate processes); `lru-cache` README
NODE-COR-60.fix: a shared cache (Redis) with a version key or short TTL, or no cache on mutable data.

NODE-COR-61.title: Check-then-use on the filesystem
NODE-COR-61.cite: CWE-367; Node.js docs, `fs.access` ("Using `fs.access()` to check for the accessibility of a file before calling `fs.open()`... is not recommended") and file system flags (`wx`)
NODE-COR-61.fix: attempt the operation and handle the error; the `wx` flag for exclusive creation; `fs.mkdtemp` for temporary directories.

NODE-COR-62.title: Relative ESM import without a file extension
NODE-COR-62.cite: Node.js docs, "ECMAScript modules: Mandatory file extensions"; TypeScript handbook, "Modules - Theory" (`moduleResolution: nodenext`)
NODE-COR-62.fix: write the extension (`.js` even for `.ts` sources), or compile with a tool that rewrites specifiers.

NODE-COR-63.title: CommonJS globals used in an ES module
NODE-COR-63.cite: Node.js docs, "ECMAScript modules: Differences between ES modules and CommonJS"

NODE-COR-64.title: Implicit numeric enum values that are stored or sent
NODE-COR-64.cite: TypeScript handbook, "Enums" (numeric enums, auto-incremented members); typescript-eslint, `prefer-enum-initializers`
NODE-COR-64.fix: string values (`as const` object or a string enum), or explicit initializers that are never renumbered.

NODE-COR-65.title: Middleware registered after the routes it must guard
NODE-COR-65.cite: Express docs, "Using middleware" (order of middleware loading is important); Fastify docs, "Hooks" and "Encapsulation"
NODE-COR-65.fix: register parsers and security first, routes next, the error handler last; in Fastify, scope hooks to a plugin that contains the routes.

NODE-COR-66.title: Logger called with the fields in the wrong position
NODE-COR-66.cite: Pino docs, "API: logger" (`logger.info([mergingObject], [message], [...interpolationValues])`); Pino docs, "Pino standard serializers" (`err`)
NODE-COR-66.fix: object first, message second; the error under the `err` key.

NODE-COR-67.title: Environment value used without parsing
NODE-COR-67.cite: MDN, `Number()` (`Number(undefined)` is `NaN`, `Number('')` is `0`); Twelve-Factor App, III Config
NODE-COR-67.fix: parse and validate all variables once at start-up and fail fast.

NODE-COR-68.title: Query on a soft-deleted model without the `deletedAt` filter
NODE-COR-68.cite: Prisma docs, "Client extensions" (query component); CWE-212 (improper removal of sensitive information)
NODE-COR-68.fix: add the filter, or enforce it in one place (a Prisma client extension or a view).

NODE-COR-69.title: "First" row taken without a deterministic order
NODE-COR-69.cite: PostgreSQL docs, "Sorting Rows" (`ORDER BY`; without it the order is unspecified)
NODE-COR-69.fix: add an `orderBy` that defines the intended row, or `findUnique` on a unique key.

NODE-COR-70.title: Repeatable job registered on every start without a stable id
NODE-COR-70.fix: an idempotent registration (`upsertJobScheduler`, or a stable `jobId`), done by one process.

NODE-COR-71.title: Breaking change to an existing public route
NODE-COR-71.cite: RFC 9745 (the `Deprecation` HTTP response header field); RFC 8594 (the `Sunset` header field)
NODE-COR-71.fix: add fields instead of changing them; version the route for a breaking change; announce deprecation.

NODE-DIFF-01.title: Debug output or debugger left in
NODE-DIFF-01.fix: delete it, or use the project logger at `debug` level with no secrets.

NODE-ERR-01.title: Swallowed exception
NODE-ERR-01.fix: catch the specific error; log with context; re-raise or return an explicit failure type the caller must handle.

NODE-ERR-02.title: Over-broad catch or try body
NODE-ERR-02.cite: PEP 8, "Programming Recommendations" (limit the `try` clause; avoid bare `except`)
NODE-ERR-02.fix: one risky call per `try`; catch the specific class; re-raise the rest; never catch `BaseException` without re-raising `CancelledError`.

NODE-ERR-03.title: Lost cause and stack
NODE-ERR-03.fix: `logging.exception` / `exc_info=True`; `raise … from err`; `new Error(msg, { cause })`; log the error object under the logger's `err` key.

NODE-ERR-04.title: Unchecked I/O result, no timeout
NODE-ERR-04.cite: WHATWG Fetch Standard (the promise rejects only on network errors); MDN, `Response.ok` and `AbortSignal.timeout()`
NODE-ERR-04.fix: a timeout on every outbound call; check the status; validate the body at the boundary; decide what the caller sees on each failure.

NODE-ERR-05.title: Wrong status code or error shape
NODE-ERR-05.cite: RFC 9457 (problem details); RFC 9110 §15 (4xx client errors, 5xx server errors)
NODE-ERR-05.fix: validate at the boundary and return 400/422; map domain errors to 4xx in one handler; use one problem shape across routes.

NODE-ERR-06.title: Cleanup missing on the error path
NODE-ERR-06.cite: Python docs, "The with statement" and `contextlib`; node-postgres docs, "Pooling" (a checked-out client must be released)
NODE-ERR-06.fix: `with` / `try … finally`; `pipeline()` for streams; `contextlib.closing` for objects without a context manager; roll back in the error path.

NODE-ERR-07.title: Multi-step write with no transaction
NODE-ERR-07.fix: one transaction for the writes; record intent before the external call and the result after; an outbox for events; make the sequence resumable and idempotent.

NODE-ERR-08.title: Background failure never observed
NODE-ERR-08.cite: Python docs, `asyncio.create_task` and "Developing with asyncio" (task exceptions never retrieved); Node.js docs, `process` "unhandledRejection" (default `throw` since v15)
NODE-ERR-08.fix: keep the task reference and log failures in a done callback; wrap async handlers (or use Express 5 / Fastify, which handle them); attach `.catch` at every event-emitter boundary.

NODE-ERR-10.title: Retry without bound, backoff or filter
NODE-ERR-10.cite: AWS Builders' Library, "Timeouts, retries, and backoff with jitter"; Google SRE Book, "Addressing Cascading Failures"
NODE-ERR-10.fix: a maximum attempt count, exponential backoff with jitter, retry only transient errors, raise after the last attempt; use the library's retry policy (tenacity, p-retry) once.

NODE-ERR-52.title: `schema.parse()` of client input with the error left unmapped
NODE-ERR-52.cite: Zod docs, "Basic usage" (`parse` throws, `safeParse` returns); RFC 9457
NODE-ERR-52.fix: `safeParse` and return 400/422, or register one error handler that maps `ZodError`.

NODE-ERR-53.title: EventEmitter listener added per call and never removed
NODE-ERR-53.cite: Node.js docs, `events` ("Possible EventEmitter memory leak", `emitter.off`); CWE-401
NODE-ERR-53.fix: remove the listener when the request or connection ends; `once` where it fires once.

NODE-ERR-54.title: `uncaughtException` or `unhandledRejection` handler that keeps running
NODE-ERR-54.cite: Node.js docs, `process` event `'uncaughtException'` (it is not safe to resume normal operation after it)
NODE-ERR-54.fix: log, close the server with a deadline and exit non-zero.

NODE-ERR-56.title: Job added without attempts or backoff
NODE-ERR-56.cite: BullMQ docs, "Retrying failing jobs"; AWS Builders' Library, "Timeouts, retries and backoff with jitter"
NODE-ERR-56.fix: set `attempts` and exponential `backoff` (in `defaultJobOptions` for the whole queue) and make the handler idempotent.

NODE-MAINT-01.title: Unused import, variable or parameter
NODE-MAINT-01.fix: `ruff check --fix`; remove the parameter and update the callers.

NODE-MAINT-02.title: Name that misleads
NODE-MAINT-02.cite: Google Engineering Practices, "Naming" (a name should say what the thing is or does); Martin, *Clean Code* ch. 2 (names)
NODE-MAINT-02.fix: rename (or split) so the name states the effect and the unit; a rename is cheap now and costly after merge.

NODE-MAINT-03.title: Dead or unreachable code
NODE-MAINT-03.cite: CWE-561 (dead code); CWE-570 and CWE-571 (always false, always true)
NODE-MAINT-03.fix: delete it; version control keeps the history.

NODE-MAINT-04.title: Duplicated rule that will drift
NODE-MAINT-04.cite: Hunt and Thomas, *The Pragmatic Programmer* (DRY: every piece of knowledge has a single authoritative representation); Metz, "The Wrong Abstraction"
NODE-MAINT-04.fix: call the existing function or extract one; leave similar-looking but unrelated code alone. Do not merge incidental duplicates: the wrong abstraction costs more than the copy.

NODE-MAINT-05.title: Layering leak
NODE-MAINT-05.cite: Google Engineering Practices, "Design"; import-linter docs, "Contract types"
NODE-MAINT-05.fix: pass values in, not the request; move the query to the repository or the data hook; enforce the boundary with a lint rule rather than a review comment.

NODE-MAINT-06.title: Magic value
NODE-MAINT-06.cite: Martin, *Clean Code* G25 (replace magic numbers with named constants); CWE-1106 (insufficient use of symbolic constants)
NODE-MAINT-06.fix: named constants (or an enum) with the unit in the name; config for values that change per environment.

NODE-MAINT-07.title: Over-complex changed function
NODE-MAINT-07.cite: McCabe, "A Complexity Measure" (IEEE Trans. Software Eng., 1976); Google Engineering Practices, "Complexity"
NODE-MAINT-07.fix: extract named steps; replace flag arguments with an options object or separate functions; use a lookup table for branching on a value.

NODE-MAINT-08.title: Types erased at a boundary
NODE-MAINT-08.fix: annotate the public surface; replace ignores with fixes; parse external data into a type at the boundary instead of asserting it.

NODE-MAINT-09.title: Comment or docstring contradicts the code
NODE-MAINT-09.fix: change the code or the comment so they agree; prefer deleting a comment that restates the code.

NODE-MAINT-53.title: Compiler or linter strictness weakened
NODE-MAINT-53.fix: keep the flag on and fix the errors; scope a necessary exception to one file with a comment that explains why.

NODE-MAINT-58.title: Log message built by interpolation
NODE-MAINT-58.cite: Pino docs, "Child loggers" and "API: logger"; OWASP Logging Cheat Sheet

NODE-MAINT-59.title: Library code creates or configures a logger
NODE-MAINT-59.cite: Node.js docs, `diagnostics_channel` (library-neutral diagnostics); OpenTelemetry docs, "Libraries" (instrumentation for libraries must not own the exporter)
NODE-MAINT-59.fix: accept an optional `logger` parameter with a no-op default.

NODE-OPS-01.title: Container runs as root
NODE-OPS-01.cite: Docker docs, "Dockerfile best practices" (`USER`); OWASP Docker Security Cheat Sheet, Rule #2

NODE-OPS-02.title: Mutable base image or non-reproducible install
NODE-OPS-02.cite: Docker docs, "Dockerfile best practices"; npm docs, `npm ci`
NODE-OPS-02.fix: pin the image tag or digest; `npm ci` with the lockfile.

NODE-OPS-03.title: Build leftovers in the runtime image
NODE-OPS-03.cite: Docker docs, "Multi-stage builds" and "Dockerfile best practices"

NODE-OPS-04.title: Health endpoint that lies
NODE-OPS-04.cite: Kubernetes docs, "Configure Liveness, Readiness and Startup Probes"
NODE-OPS-04.fix: liveness checks the process; readiness checks required dependencies and returns 503.

NODE-OPS-05.title: SIGTERM handler exits without draining
NODE-OPS-05.fix: stop accepting connections, finish in-flight work, close pools, then exit.

NODE-OPS-06.title: Unsafe schema change in the deploy path
NODE-OPS-06.cite: Prisma docs, "Deploying database changes with Prisma Migrate" (`migrate deploy` in production, `migrate dev` in development) and "Prototyping with db push"
NODE-OPS-06.fix: `prisma migrate deploy` once per release before the new version starts; split destructive changes into a later release.

NODE-OPS-07.title: Development log transport enabled in production
NODE-OPS-07.cite: Pino docs, "Pretty Printing" (for development; use JSON in production)
NODE-OPS-07.fix: pretty output only when explicitly enabled for local development.

NODE-OPS-08.title: `keepAliveTimeout` shorter than the load balancer's idle timeout
NODE-OPS-08.cite: Node.js docs, `server.keepAliveTimeout` (default 5000 ms); AWS docs, "Application Load Balancer: idle timeout" (default 60 s)
NODE-OPS-08.fix: set `keepAliveTimeout` above the proxy idle timeout and `headersTimeout` above that.

NODE-PERF-01.title: Query or remote call per item (N+1)
NODE-PERF-01.fix: `select_related` (to-one) / `prefetch_related` (to-many) / `selectinload` / `include`; `WHERE id IN (…)`; a DataLoader per request in GraphQL; a batch endpoint for the browser.

NODE-PERF-02.title: Blocking call in async or request code
NODE-PERF-02.cite: Node.js docs, "Don't Block the Event Loop (or the Worker Pool)"; Python docs, `asyncio` "Running blocking code" and `asyncio.to_thread`
NODE-PERF-02.fix: the async API of the same library; `asyncio.to_thread` / `run_in_executor`; worker threads for CPU work in Node.

NODE-PERF-04.title: Unbounded concurrency
NODE-PERF-04.cite: CWE-770 (allocation of resources without limits); CWE-400
NODE-PERF-04.fix: a concurrency limit (`p-limit`, `Semaphore`), batches, a queue; cap the input size.

NODE-PERF-05.title: Unbounded memory
NODE-PERF-05.fix: stream; paginate with a hard cap; `maxsize` and TTL on caches; limit body size at the framework.

NODE-PERF-06.title: Quadratic loops
NODE-PERF-06.fix: build a `set` / `dict` / `Map` once; `collections.deque` for queues; push into one accumulator instead of copying.

NODE-PERF-07.title: Query shape: scan, deep offset, over-fetch
NODE-PERF-07.cite: PostgreSQL docs, "Indexes" (Index Types, Indexes on Expressions, Indexes and ORDER BY); Django docs, `QuerySet.exists()`
NODE-PERF-07.fix: add the index in the same change; `.exists()` / `EXISTS`; keyset pagination; select only the columns the view uses; `pg_trgm` for substring search.

NODE-PERF-08.title: Client or connection created per request
NODE-PERF-08.cite: node-postgres docs, "Pooling"; SQLAlchemy docs, "Engine Configuration" (one engine per database URL per process)
NODE-PERF-08.fix: build the client at module or application scope and inject it; close it on shutdown.

NODE-PERF-11.title: Catastrophic regex backtracking
NODE-PERF-11.cite: CWE-1333; OWASP, "Regular expression Denial of Service (ReDoS)"
NODE-PERF-11.fix: rewrite so each character can match one way; cap the input length first; use RE2 (`google-re2`, `re2`) for user-supplied patterns or when the pattern cannot be simplified.

NODE-PERF-54.title: Response serialized by hand in Fastify
NODE-PERF-54.cite: Fastify docs, "Validation and Serialization" (response schema serialization)
NODE-PERF-54.fix: return the object and declare a response schema.

NODE-PERF-55.title: Unbounded metric label cardinality
NODE-PERF-55.cite: Prometheus docs, "Instrumentation" and "Metric and label naming"; prom-client README
NODE-PERF-55.fix: route template and status only; ids go to logs and traces.

NODE-SEC-01.title: SQL text built from request input
NODE-SEC-01.fix: bound parameters (`?`, `%s`, `$1`, `:name`) or the ORM query builder; allowlist identifiers.

NODE-SEC-02.title: Secret literal in source or in the client bundle
NODE-SEC-02.fix: environment or secret manager, fail fast when missing; browser calls go through an own backend route; **rotate** the leaked value (removing it from the code does not un-leak it).

NODE-SEC-03.title: Request-controlled path reaches the filesystem
NODE-SEC-03.cite: CWE-22; OWASP A01:2021 Broken Access Control
NODE-SEC-03.fix: Flask `send_from_directory`, Werkzeug `secure_filename`; `resolve()` plus `is_relative_to` / `startsWith(base + path.sep)`; `tarfile` extraction filters; server-generated storage names.

NODE-SEC-04.title: Object read or changed by a client-supplied ID without an ownership check
NODE-SEC-04.fix: scope every query by the owner or tenant taken from the session; return 404 on a miss; keep the rule in one policy helper.

NODE-SEC-05.title: Redirect target taken from the request
NODE-SEC-05.cite: CWE-601; OWASP A01:2021 Broken Access Control
NODE-SEC-05.fix: allowlist, or parse with a real URL parser against the own origin and compare origins; Django `url_has_allowed_host_and_scheme`; the same in Node with `new URL(next, base)`.

NODE-SEC-06.title: State change reachable cross-site with cookie authentication (CSRF)
NODE-SEC-06.cite: CWE-352; OWASP A01:2021 Broken Access Control
NODE-SEC-06.fix: state changes only on unsafe methods; a synchronizer or signed double-submit token (Flask-WTF `CSRFProtect`, Django `CsrfViewMiddleware`, `@fastify/csrf-protection`); `SameSite` as defense in depth, n

NODE-SEC-07.title: Non-cryptographic random used for a security value

NODE-SEC-08.title: Password stored with a fast, unsalted or reversible hash
NODE-SEC-08.fix: Argon2id, scrypt, bcrypt or PBKDF2 with the parameters in the OWASP Password Storage Cheat Sheet; rehash on next login.

NODE-SEC-09.title: CORS reflects any origin with credentials
NODE-SEC-09.fix: exact-match allowlist of origins; credentials only for those.

NODE-SEC-10.title: Secret or MAC compared with a non-constant-time operator
NODE-SEC-10.fix: `hmac.compare_digest`; `crypto.timingSafeEqual` on equal-length buffers (hash both sides first, since it throws on a length mismatch).

NODE-SEC-11.title: JWT accepted without signature, algorithm or expiry verification
NODE-SEC-11.fix: verify with a fixed algorithm allowlist, issuer and audience; require `exp`; never branch on decoded-but-unverified claims on the server.

NODE-SEC-12.title: TLS certificate verification disabled
NODE-SEC-12.fix: trust the private CA explicitly instead of disabling verification.

NODE-SEC-13.title: NoSQL operator injection
NODE-SEC-13.fix: schema-validate scalar types; `$eq` for user values; Mongoose `sanitizeFilter`.

NODE-SEC-14.title: Shell command built from input
NODE-SEC-14.fix: argument list without a shell; `--` before user operands; validate scheme and format (`https://` only).

NODE-SEC-15.title: Input evaluated as code
NODE-SEC-15.fix: `ast.literal_eval`, a parser with an operator allowlist, or a `Map` of permitted operations; never `vm` for untrusted code.

NODE-SEC-16.title: User-controlled text rendered as HTML
NODE-SEC-16.fix: render as text; sanitize with DOMPurify when HTML is required; autoescaping templates with user data as context, never as template source.

NODE-SEC-17.title: Price, amount or entitlement taken from the client
NODE-SEC-17.fix: take only identifiers and quantities from the client; look up prices and entitlements on the server; bound quantities.

NODE-SEC-18.title: Debug mode or internal error detail exposed
NODE-SEC-18.fix: log the detail server-side with a request ID; return a generic problem response.

NODE-SEC-19.title: Auth cookie set without `HttpOnly` or `Secure`
NODE-SEC-19.fix: `HttpOnly`, `Secure`, `SameSite=Lax` (or `Strict`) on every auth cookie; scope the path of refresh cookies.

NODE-SEC-20.title: Authentication or authorization check not awaited
NODE-SEC-20.fix: `await` the check; enable `no-misused-promises` (type-aware) and mypy `truthy-bool`; treat "coroutine … was never awaited" warnings as errors in tests.

NODE-SEC-21.title: Untrusted data deserialized into objects or code
NODE-SEC-21.cite: CWE-502; OWASP A08:2021 Software and Data Integrity Failures
NODE-SEC-21.fix: JSON plus schema validation; `yaml.safe_load`; `weights_only=True`; sign data that must round-trip and still avoid pickle.

NODE-SEC-22.title: Request body written to a model wholesale (mass assignment)
NODE-SEC-22.fix: an input schema that lists writable fields; copy fields explicitly; no deep merge of request data into shared objects (use `Object.create(null)` or `Map` when merging is needed).

NODE-SEC-23.title: Secrets or personal data written to logs or telemetry
NODE-SEC-23.cite: CWE-532; OWASP A09:2021 Security Logging and Monitoring Failures
NODE-SEC-23.fix: log identifiers, not values; configure redaction (Pino `redact`); allowlist the properties sent to telemetry.

NODE-SEC-24.title: Security check fails open or its failure leaves no record
NODE-SEC-24.fix: deny inside the handler of a failed check; log security failures at `warning` with the event name and source, never the secret.

NODE-SEC-25.title: Server fetches a URL the caller controls
NODE-SEC-25.cite: CWE-918; OWASP A10:2021 Server-Side Request Forgery
NODE-SEC-25.fix: host allowlist; when arbitrary hosts are a feature (webhooks), resolve and block private ranges at connect time or use an egress proxy; disable redirects; do not return the raw response.

NODE-SEC-53.title: Refresh token not rotated, not revocable, or stored in clear
NODE-SEC-53.cite: RFC 9700 (OAuth 2.0 Security BCP) §4.14 (refresh token protection); OWASP Session Management Cheat Sheet
NODE-SEC-53.fix: rotate on every use; store only a hash; revoke the whole family when an old token is presented again.

NODE-SEC-54.title: Login or reset reveals whether an account exists
NODE-SEC-54.cite: OWASP Authentication Cheat Sheet, "Authentication and error messages"; CWE-204
NODE-SEC-54.fix: one message and one status for both cases; equalize the work (hash a dummy password when the user is missing).

NODE-TEST-01.title: New or changed logic with no test
NODE-TEST-01.cite: Google Engineering Practices, "Code Review Developer Guide" ("Tests": tests should be included in the same change); pytest docs, "How to parametrize fixtures and test functions"
NODE-TEST-01.fix: name the cases the test must cover (each branch, one boundary, one failure); suggest the test, do not write the whole suite.

NODE-TEST-02.title: Vacuous test: asserts nothing real
NODE-TEST-02.cite: pytest docs, "Asserting with the `assert` statement" and "Assertions about expected exceptions"; Jest docs, `.resolves` / `.rejects` (return or await the assertion)
NODE-TEST-02.fix: assert the specific value, status or message; await promise matchers; assert on the outcome the user cares about.

NODE-TEST-03.title: Self-confirming expected value
NODE-TEST-03.cite: Google Testing Blog, "Testing on the Toilet: Test Behavior, Not Implementation"; Jest docs, "Snapshot Testing" (snapshots are reviewed as code)
NODE-TEST-03.fix: hard-code expected values taken from the spec or a worked example; review snapshots line by line.

NODE-TEST-04.title: Over-mocking
NODE-TEST-04.cite: Google Testing Blog, "Testing on the Toilet: Don't Overuse Mocks"; Martin Fowler, "Mocks Aren't Stubs"
NODE-TEST-04.fix: mock at the system boundary (network, clock, third-party SDK), use fakes or an in-memory database for your own layers, add `autospec` / typed mocks, and patch where the name is looked up.

NODE-TEST-05.title: Flaky patterns
NODE-TEST-05.cite: Martin Fowler, "Eradicating Non-Determinism in Tests"; Google Testing Blog, "Flaky Tests at Google and How We Mitigate Them"
NODE-TEST-05.fix: wait on a condition (`findBy*`, events), inject or freeze the clock, seed randomness, sort before comparing, fake the network.

NODE-TEST-06.title: Disabled, focused or weakened test

TS-ACC-09.fix: native elements first; ARIA only for what HTML cannot express.

TS-COR-01.title: Module-level mutable state shared across requests or users
TS-COR-01.cite: TanStack Query docs, "Advanced Server Rendering" (create the `QueryClient` per request to avoid sharing data between users); Zustand docs, "Setup with Next.js" (no global store on the server)
TS-COR-01.fix: create the client or store inside the request (or in a provider's `useState` on the client); never keep per-user data in module scope on the server.

TS-COR-02.title: Duplicable external effect without an idempotency key
TS-COR-02.fix: an `Idempotency-Key` derived from the business object (not random per attempt); record the attempt before calling; a unique constraint or processed-events table; disable the button while pending.

TS-COR-03.title: In-place mutation and aliasing of caller-owned data
TS-COR-03.cite: Python docs, `list.sort` (sorts in place, returns `None`); Python Programming FAQ, "How do I create a multidimensional list?"
TS-COR-03.fix: `sorted()` / `toSorted()` / spread / `structuredClone` for nested data; build rows with a comprehension; filter into a new list instead of removing while iterating.

TS-COR-04.title: Absent value dereferenced
TS-COR-04.cite: Python docs, `re.match` (returns `None` when no match); MDN, `Array.prototype.find` (returns `undefined`)
TS-COR-04.fix: check and return 404/422, or `next(it, default)`; enable `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`; replace `!` with a real check.

TS-COR-05.title: Falsy value treated as missing
TS-COR-05.cite: Python docs, "Truth Value Testing"; MDN, "Nullish coalescing operator (??)" and "Logical OR (||)"
TS-COR-05.fix: compare to `None` / `undefined`; use `??`; parse flags explicitly.

TS-COR-06.title: Boundary and pagination off-by-one
TS-COR-06.cite: CWE-193 (off-by-one error); Python docs, "Common Sequence Operations" (slicing)
TS-COR-06.fix: iterate over elements, not indexes; half-open ranges; fetch `size + 1` rows to detect a next page.

TS-COR-07.title: Time zones and date arithmetic
TS-COR-07.cite: Python docs, `datetime` ("Aware and Naive Objects") and "What's New in Python 3.12" (`utcnow` deprecation); PEP 615 (`zoneinfo`)
TS-COR-07.fix: store and compare aware UTC instants; convert to the user's zone only for display (`zoneinfo`, `Intl.DateTimeFormat`); add calendar units with a library; `monotonic()` for durations.

TS-COR-08.title: Floating point money
TS-COR-08.cite: Python docs, "Floating Point Arithmetic: Issues and Limitations" and `decimal`; ECMA-262, Number type (IEEE 754 binary64)
TS-COR-08.fix: integer minor units end to end, or `Decimal` built from strings with an explicit quantize and rounding mode; a decimal column in the database.

TS-COR-10.title: Async work not awaited
TS-COR-10.cite: Python docs, `asyncio.create_task` (save a reference to avoid a task disappearing mid-execution); Python docs, "Coroutines and Tasks"
TS-COR-10.fix: `await` it, `Promise.all` it, or keep the task reference and attach a done callback that logs; `for … of` with `await` when order matters.

TS-COR-11.title: Stale closure and effect dependencies
TS-COR-11.cite: React docs, "Synchronizing with Effects", "Removing Effect Dependencies", "Queueing a Series of State Updates"
TS-COR-11.fix: list every reactive value; use the functional updater; move non-reactive values out of the component; let the lint rule drive the list and remove disables.

TS-COR-12.title: Out-of-order responses and effect cleanup
TS-COR-12.cite: React docs, "Synchronizing with Effects" (fetching data, cleanup, Strict Mode); MDN, `AbortController`
TS-COR-12.fix: `AbortController` or an `ignore` flag; a cleanup function for everything the effect starts; prefer a data library (TanStack Query) that handles cancellation and caching.

TS-COR-13.title: Redundant state and wrong list keys
TS-COR-13.cite: React docs, "Rendering Lists" (keys), "Choosing the State Structure", "You Might Not Need an Effect"
TS-COR-13.fix: derive in render; reset with `key`; use stable ids from the data.

TS-COR-14.title: Comparison semantics

TS-COR-14.fix: numeric comparator; test membership in a collection; `==` for values, `is` only for `None` and singletons.

TS-COR-16.title: Cache key missing a dimension
TS-COR-16.cite: TanStack Query docs, "Query Keys"; RFC 9111 §4.1 (`Vary`) and §5.2.2.7 (`private`)
TS-COR-16.fix: include every input in the key; do not cache per-user responses in shared caches; `Cache-Control: private` plus `Vary` for HTTP; call `invalidateQueries` after mutations.

TS-COR-72.title: Number or string on the left of `&&` in JSX
TS-COR-72.cite: React docs, "Conditional Rendering" (do not put numbers on the left side of `&&`)
TS-COR-72.fix: make the condition a boolean (`> 0`, `Boolean(x)`, `!!x`), or use a ternary.

TS-COR-73.title: Hook called conditionally, or a hook not named `use*`
TS-COR-73.cite: React docs, "Rules of Hooks"; React docs, "Reusing Logic with Custom Hooks" (names starting with `use`)
TS-COR-73.fix: call hooks unconditionally at the top level; rename wrappers to `use*`.

TS-COR-74.title: Server-only module reachable from client code
TS-COR-74.cite: Next.js docs, "Server and Client Components: Keeping server-only code out of the client environment" (the `server-only` package)
TS-COR-74.fix: add `import 'server-only'` to server modules; pass data to client components as props; call a Server Action or API route from the client.

TS-COR-75.title: Effect used to run the logic of a user action
TS-COR-75.cite: React docs, "You Might Not Need an Effect" (sending a POST request on user action); React docs, "Synchronizing with Effects" (Strict Mode re-runs effects in development)
TS-COR-75.fix: put the logic in the event handler (or a mutation); keep effects for synchronization.

TS-COR-76.title: Query runs with a missing parameter

TS-COR-77.title: Client environment variable read dynamically
TS-COR-77.cite: Next.js docs, "Environment Variables: Bundling Environment Variables for the Browser" (dynamic lookups are not inlined)
TS-COR-77.fix: reference each variable by its full literal name; validate once in a module.

TS-COR-78.title: Path alias declared in one place only
TS-COR-78.cite: TypeScript handbook, "Modules - Reference: `paths`" (`paths` does not change emitted specifiers); Vite docs, `resolve.alias`
TS-COR-78.fix: mirror the alias in every tool that resolves imports (bundler, test runner, linter resolver), or use a plugin that reads `tsconfig.json`.

TS-DIFF-01.title: Debug output or debugger left in
TS-DIFF-01.fix: delete it, or use the project logger at `debug` level with no secrets.

TS-ERR-01.title: Swallowed exception
TS-ERR-01.fix: catch the specific error; log with context; re-raise or return an explicit failure type the caller must handle.

TS-ERR-03.title: Lost cause and stack
TS-ERR-03.fix: `logging.exception` / `exc_info=True`; `raise … from err`; `new Error(msg, { cause })`; log the error object under the logger's `err` key.

TS-ERR-04.title: Unchecked I/O result, no timeout

TS-ERR-04.fix: a timeout on every outbound call; check the status; validate the body at the boundary; decide what the caller sees on each failure.

TS-ERR-10.title: Retry without bound, backoff or filter
TS-ERR-10.cite: AWS Builders' Library, "Timeouts, retries, and backoff with jitter"; Google SRE Book, "Addressing Cascading Failures"
TS-ERR-10.fix: a maximum attempt count, exponential backoff with jitter, retry only transient errors, raise after the last attempt; use the library's retry policy (tenacity, p-retry) once.

TS-ERR-11.title: UI error and loading state
TS-ERR-11.cite: React docs, "Catching rendering errors with an error boundary" (boundaries do not catch event-handler or async errors); TanStack Query docs, "Queries" (`isError`, `error`)
TS-ERR-11.fix: `try / catch / finally`; render an error state; use the query library's `isError`; add error boundaries and `error.tsx` for render and route failures.

TS-ERR-52.title: `schema.parse()` of a network response outside error handling

TS-ERR-52.fix: `safeParse` and a defined failure path, or `parse` inside the `queryFn` so the query's error state shows it.

TS-ERR-55.title: Optimistic update without rollback or settle
TS-ERR-55.fix: snapshot in `onMutate`, restore in `onError`, invalidate in `onSettled`.

TS-MAINT-01.title: Unused import, variable or parameter
TS-MAINT-01.fix: `ruff check --fix`; remove the parameter and update the callers.

TS-MAINT-02.title: Name that misleads

TS-MAINT-02.fix: rename (or split) so the name states the effect and the unit; a rename is cheap now and costly after merge.

TS-MAINT-03.title: Dead or unreachable code
TS-MAINT-03.cite: CWE-561 (dead code); CWE-570 and CWE-571 (always false, always true)
TS-MAINT-03.fix: delete it; version control keeps the history.

TS-MAINT-04.fix: call the existing function or extract one; leave similar-looking but unrelated code alone. Do not merge incidental duplicates: the wrong abstraction costs more than the copy.

TS-MAINT-05.cite: Google Engineering Practices, "Design"; import-linter docs, "Contract types"
TS-MAINT-05.fix: pass values in, not the request; move the query to the repository or the data hook; enforce the boundary with a lint rule rather than a review comment.

TS-MAINT-06.title: Magic value
TS-MAINT-06.cite: Martin, *Clean Code* G25 (replace magic numbers with named constants); CWE-1106 (insufficient use of symbolic constants)
TS-MAINT-06.fix: named constants (or an enum) with the unit in the name; config for values that change per environment.

TS-MAINT-07.title: Over-complex changed function
TS-MAINT-07.cite: McCabe, "A Complexity Measure" (IEEE Trans. Software Eng., 1976); Google Engineering Practices, "Complexity"
TS-MAINT-07.fix: extract named steps; replace flag arguments with an options object or separate functions; use a lookup table for branching on a value.

TS-MAINT-08.title: Types erased at a boundary
TS-MAINT-08.fix: annotate the public surface; replace ignores with fixes; parse external data into a type at the boundary instead of asserting it.

TS-MAINT-09.title: Comment or docstring contradicts the code
TS-MAINT-09.fix: change the code or the comment so they agree; prefer deleting a comment that restates the code.

TS-MAINT-53.title: Compiler or linter strictness weakened
TS-MAINT-53.fix: keep the flag on and fix the errors; scope a necessary exception to one file with the reason.

TS-MAINT-60.title: Hard-coded design value where the project has tokens

TS-MAINT-60.fix: use the token; add one if the value is genuinely new.

TS-MAINT-61.fix: neutral placeholders for logos, names and copy; substitute open fonts for commercial ones.

TS-PERF-06.fix: build a `set` / `dict` / `Map` once; `collections.deque` for queues; push into one accumulator instead of copying.

TS-PERF-09.fix: hoist components and constants; `useMemo` / `useCallback` only where a memoized child or a measured computation needs it; move state down; paginate or virtualize (`react-window`).

TS-SEC-04.fix: scope every query by the owner or tenant taken from the session; return 404 on a miss; keep the rule in one policy helper.

TS-SEC-17.fix: take only identifiers and quantities from the client; look up prices and entitlements on the server; bound quantities.

TS-SEC-20.fix: `await` the check; enable `no-misused-promises` (type-aware) and mypy `truthy-bool`; treat "coroutine … was never awaited" warnings as errors in tests.
